cards.text: This is a psalm of David, king of Israel, a song for the dedication of the temple. David's talking straight to the LORD, and he opens with, "I will exalt You, O LORD," because the LORD lifted him up. Friend, NOBODY appreciates getting lifted up like a stamper who spent years in the back of a junk drawer.

cards.question: The LORD lifted David up. What does David say the LORD didn't let his foes do?

cards.text: Then David tells how it went down. He was hurting, and he didn't send a polite little text, friend, he CRIED to the LORD for help.

cards.question: David cried to the LORD for help, and the LORD ___ him.

cards.text: Then David goes even deeper. He says the LORD pulled him up from Sheol, the place of the dead.

cards.question: The LORD pulled David up from Sheol. What else does David say the LORD spared him from?

cards.text: Then David calls out to the LORD's saints: "Sing to the LORD, O you His saints, and praise His holy name." He went from crying for help to LEADING THE CHOIR.

cards.question: David tells the saints about the LORD: His anger is ___, but His favor lasts a lifetime.
David has another line for the saints: "Weeping may stay the night, but joy comes in the morning." True or false: he means sorrow won't last forever and joy is on its way.

cards.text: Now David gets honest about himself. There was a time he said, "I will never be shaken."

cards.question: David once said, "I will never be shaken." When does he say he talked like that?

cards.text: Back then, the LORD had favored David and made his mountain stand strong. Strong. Steady. Life was GOOD.

cards.question: The LORD had made David's mountain stand strong. True or false: when the LORD hid His face, David stayed just as steady as before.

cards.text: David calls to the LORD and begs for mercy. Then he makes his case like it's closing arguments.

cards.question: David asks the LORD what gain there is in his going down to the Pit. Then he asks, "Will the dust praise You?" What's his point?

answers.text: If he dies he can't praise the LORD
Even dust will praise the LORD someday
His foes are worth no more than dust

cards.text: Then David boils it all down: hear me, have mercy, be my helper. No fancy speech this time, friend, just HELP.
And David says the LORD turned his mourning into DANCING. Friend, when good news hits me, I'm hopping around on this gold base like the oven timer just went off.

cards.question: The LORD peeled off David's sackcloth and clothed him with ___.
David's sackcloth is gone. Why does he say the LORD turned his mourning into dancing?

answers.text: So his heart would sing and not be silent
So his foes would see it and be ashamed
So the people would follow him to battle

cards.question: David closes by talking to the LORD. True or false: he says he'll give thanks until his troubles are over.
